newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says liquidation rules to protect savers.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says liquidation rules to protect savers.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank said on Monday the government's new regulation on bank liquidation was aimed at improving protection for depositors.

"The regulation is a preventive tool and will provide clearer ways on how to handle a bank liquidation. So that there will be no more doubts in in the handling of such a case," Bank Indonesia's Managing Director Hendrobudiyanto told a news conference.

Central bank director Heru Soepraptomo said the regulation, signed into effect by President Suharto on December 3, includes details regarding the revoking of a bank's business license and the setting up and management of a liquidation team.

Both Hendrobudiyanto and Heru Soepraptomo declined to comment whether the regulation was a warning to some of the country's banks which had allegedly failed to meet the monetary authority's requirements.
Heru said the rule stipulated that savers will be given priority in the event of a bank's liquidation after the clearing of unpaid salaries of employees, auction fees, tax and administrative fees.
"The new regulation offers clearer and higher priority for depositors compared with the previous one," Heru said adding depositors were not on the priority list in the past.
Heru said the government had revoked and liquidated more than 50 small and large banks since the country's independence in 1945. -- Jakarta newsroom 6221 384-6364
